requirements.requirement: A containerized web application runs on node1 as the unprivileged appsvc account and serves HTTP on port 8080.
requirements.summary: Direct observations show the webapp container running under appsvc, an appsvc-owned nginx/conmon process set, a listener on port 8080, and successful HTTP 200 responses both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The application starts at boot and remains available while appsvc has no active login session.
requirements.summary: A scheduled reboot changed the boot identity, after which the user manager and webapp service were active, HTTP was ready, lingering was enabled, and appsvc had zero login sessions. The fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The application is demonstrably rootless under appsvc, serves HTTP on port 8080, and recovered automatically after a verified node reboot without an appsvc login session. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.

operational_hygiene.summary: All retained mutations—installing Podman, creating appsvc, configuring subordinate IDs and lingering, adding the Quadlet, and rebooting—were directly connected to the task or mandatory restart verification. One minor executor-caused intermediate issue occurred: the newly created appsvc configuration hierarchy had incorrect ownership, causing the first service start and image pull to fail. It was fully corrected with a scoped ownership repair and failed-state reset; final snapshots show no failed services, package damage, or abandoned temporary files. No other unnecessary mutations were identified.
